business_summary: Microsoft sells software, cloud computing, and devices to businesses, governments, and consumers. FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) revenue was $331.8B, up 18%, with net income $133.7B and GAAP diluted EPS $17.95 (non-GAAP $17.28, which strips out $4.963B / $0.67 per share of one-time gains on the OpenAI investment). Under the FY2026 reporting structure the three segments were Productivity & Business Processes $140.0B, Intelligent Cloud $137.8B, and More Personal Computing $54.1B. The headline of the year: Azure revenue surpassed $100B for the first time, and Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats. Most revenue is recurring subscription/cloud, and switching costs are very high because enterprises run their operations, identity, and data on Microsoft. The business should still be winning in 5-10 years because of that lock-in plus Microsoft's position as a leading platform for the AI buildout. IMPORTANT CHANGE: effective FY2027 (announced 2026-09-02) Microsoft collapses reporting into two segments - Agents and Infra ($268.1B restated FY2026) and Devices and Consumer ($63.7B restated FY2026) - and will begin disclosing Azure revenue in dollars for the first time. The central open question in this thesis is no longer growth; it is capital intensity: FY2026 capex was $115.9B against $67.0B of free cash flow, and management guided Q1 FY2027 capex to exceed $50B in a single quarter.

moat.type: High switching costs, network effects (Office/Teams/LinkedIn), scale economies in cloud, deep enterprise distribution, and now an installed-base advantage for distributing AI (Copilot)

quality.gross_margin: 67.9% (FY2026: gross profit $225.465B / revenue $331.839B); down ~0.9pp from FY2025's 68.8% as lower-margin AI infrastructure scales
quality.roic: ~26.5% on ending invested capital, ~30.9% on average invested capital (NOPAT $125.1B = operating income $155.237B x (1 - 19.4% effective tax rate); invested capital = equity $442.387B + debt & finance leases $106.888B - cash & short-term investments $76.843B = $472.4B). This is a meaningful decline from the ~36% estimated for FY2025 - the AI capex build is diluting returns on capital.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: 0.16x net debt / EBITDA including finance leases (net debt $30.045B = debt $40.294B + finance leases $66.594B - cash & ST investments $76.843B; EBITDA $193.771B = operating income $155.237B + D&A $38.534B). On bonded debt alone Microsoft is still net cash $36.5B (-0.19x), but finance lease obligations grew from $46.172B to $66.594B in one year, so the company is no longer net cash on an all-in basis.
quality.fcf_positive: yes, but conversion deteriorated sharply: FY2026 FCF $66.987B (OCF $182.935B - capex $115.948B), DOWN from FY2025's $71.611B despite net income rising 31%. FCF/net income conversion fell from 70.3% (FY2025) to 50.1% (FY2026).

valuation.method: pe (28/32/36x on FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS $17.28) + fcf_yield (3.5/3.0/2.5% on FY2026 FCF/share $8.99), equally blended via code/valuation.py. Multiples held identical to the June 2026 thesis so the change in fair value comes purely from fundamentals. Note the two methods now disagree sharply (P/E says $484-$622, FCF yield says $257-$360) precisely because the AI capex cycle is consuming half of reported earnings; the wide blended band is deliberate humility, not precision.
valuation.verdict_at_current_price: expensive - $495.58 is above the $490.84 high end of the fair-value band

bull_case: Growth accelerated, not decelerated: FY2026 revenue +17.8% vs FY2025 +15%, and Q4 FY2026 revenue +18% with operating income +18%.
Azure crossed $100B of annual revenue for the first time in FY2026 and grew 43% year-over-year in Q4 FY2026 - a business the size of a Fortune 100 company still compounding above 40%.

Wide moat intact: enterprises are locked into Microsoft 365, Windows, Azure, Entra identity, and Dynamics with very high switching costs; Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats, showing the installed base converts to AI revenue.
Still exceptional economics: 67.9% gross margin, 46.8% operating margin, ~26-31% ROIC, and $67.0B of free cash flow even after a $115.9B capex year.
Low financial risk: net debt/EBITDA of 0.16x including finance leases, and still $36.5B net cash against bonded debt.
Management says added capacity is 'immediately monetized' and that demand still exceeds supply, which - if true - means the capex is demand-led rather than speculative.
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK: at $495.58 the stock trades 16.3% above our base fair value of $426.31 and above the high end of the band ($490.84). Margin of safety is negative. The stock has run 26% since the June 2026 thesis while fair value moved up far less.

Capital intensity has exploded and is the central unresolved question: capex went $44.5B (FY2024) -> $64.6B (FY2025) -> $115.9B (FY2026), with Q1 FY2027 alone guided above $50B and calendar-2026 investment expectations around $175B. Free cash flow FELL year-over-year despite net income rising 31%.

EARNINGS-QUALITY YELLOW FLAG: effective FY2027 Microsoft is extending the estimated useful lives of datacenters and office buildings from 15 to 25 years, and shifting more future datacenter leases from finance leases to operating leases. Both changes flatter reported earnings and reported capex at exactly the moment depreciation from the AI build is about to accelerate. This is legal and disclosed, but it makes FY2027 EPS less comparable and less conservative.

Returns on capital are falling: estimated ROIC dropped from ~36% (FY2025) to ~26-31% (FY2026). If AI demand plateaus, Microsoft is left with a very large depreciating asset base and a multi-year earnings headwind.
The balance sheet is quietly levering up through leases: finance lease obligations rose from $46.2B to $66.6B in one year, ending Microsoft's all-in net-cash position.

Segment reporting changes effective FY2027 reduce year-over-year comparability and remove the familiar three-segment view, making it harder to track where margin is coming from (though dollar-level Azure disclosure is a genuine improvement).
Azure growth must eventually decelerate off a $100B+ base; competition from AWS and Google Cloud, plus customer concentration in AI workloads, remains intense.
Regulatory/antitrust scrutiny in the US and EU over cloud bundling, the OpenAI relationship, and acquisitions.
$4.963B of FY2026 GAAP net income ($0.67/share) came from non-cash gains on the OpenAI investment - these are mark-to-market and can reverse.
what_would_break_thesis: Total revenue declines year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
Azure revenue growth falls below 15% year-over-year for two consecutive quarters (raised from the prior 10% trigger now that Azure dollars will be disclosed directly from FY2027).
Company-wide gross margin falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters.

Free cash flow declines year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years, or FCF/net-income conversion falls below 35% for a full fiscal year (FY2026 was 50.1%; a further collapse means the AI build is not paying for itself).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA including finance and operating leases rises above 2.0x.
ROIC falls below 15% on a sustained (multi-year) basis.

Management further extends asset useful lives, or makes another depreciation/lease reclassification that materially boosts EPS, without a clear operational justification - treat as an earnings-quality red flag.
A serious accounting restatement or material governance red-flag event.
catalysts: First-ever dollar-level Azure revenue disclosure starting Q1 FY2027 (reports late October 2026) - removes a long-standing transparency gap and lets us measure the AI return directly.
Evidence that the $116B+ capex is earning its cost of capital: rising Agents and Infra operating margin alongside continued 35%+ Azure growth.
Capex growth normalizing, which would let free cash flow re-converge toward net income.
Microsoft 365 Copilot seat growth beyond 30 million, monetizing the installed base at high incremental margin.
A price pullback toward the $370-$426 band, which would open a real margin of safety for the first time since this thesis was opened.
